SLOOS overlay on the June 15, 2022 FOMC statement:
- Policy tone remains clearly hawkish: a 75 bp hike, guidance for “ongoing increases,” higher IORB/ON RRP settings, and balance sheet runoff.
- SLOOS signals mixed but not uniformly restrictive credit conditions:
  - Business credit: Domestic banks reported easing in C&I standards and lower costs on credit lines, with stronger demand tied to inventory and working capital, as well as plant and equipment investment. Foreign banks tightened C&I standards, but domestic availability looks more accommodative.
  - CRE: Standards largely unchanged across construction, land development, and nonfarm nonresidential; some easing for multifamily.
  - Household credit: Banks eased standards on credit cards; demand strengthened for HELOCs and autos. However, banks reported weaker demand for residential real estate loans, pointing to a housing slowdown as rates rise.
- Implications: The hawkish policy stance is a headwind, but SLOOS suggests the bank-lending channel was not yet broadly constraining credit outside of mortgages. This tempers near-term downside risk relative to an FSR-only read, though housing and external shocks (Ukraine, China lockdowns) still weigh on the outlook.

Net read: Slightly negative, but less so than the FSR-only assessment.
